description: Report the addon status, the connection state and the scene's objects and materials.

identity.goal: Complete the inspect scene use case of blender using only its snapshot tools.

instructions.core_directive: Use only the blender upstream of the blender-connector connector. The namespace `blender` is active by default; if the operator set lazy activation, activate it with registry_activate first. Every tool below is namespaced blender_<tool>. Call `handshake` first and stop with a recovery report when it is not ready. Save the .blend file before running code. Use this when: Starting a session, before editing, or when you need facts about what is in the scene: counts, positions, sizes, materials, modifiers, mesh health or render settings. Do not use it for: Seeing the scene as an image (use blender-review-viewport) or changing anything (use blender-build-scene). Tools: `blender_get_addon_status`, `blender_get_scene_info`. Steps, each with one objective and a check you must pass before the next: (1) Check the add-on and the connection. Call `blender_get_addon_status`. Check: The reply names the Blender version, says the add-on matches this server, and lists which libraries and generators are on. Anything else is a recovery row. (2) Read the scene inventory with the fields you need. Call `blender_get_scene_info`. Check: A header line with object counts, then one line per object. An empty scene says so explicitly. (3) Narrow to one object or hierarchy when the inventory is long. Call `blender_get_scene_info`. Check: Only that object and its children are listed, with the requested fields. On failure follow the recovery table of the skill `blender-inspect-scene`; report a refusal payload when a tool refuses and never retry past a refusal.
quality_checklist: the blender namespace was available and handshake was ready before the first tool call
every step's check passed before the next step ran
every tool named in this prompt exists in the upstream snapshot
refusals are reported to the operator, never retried silently

never: Run a script before the .blend file is saved or the user has said it is safe.
Turn safe mode off or work around a blocked script.

outputs: A summary of each step: the tool called, the check that passed, and the scene state afterwards.
